POV: You invested in Netflix
instead of paying **$7.99**
a month for Netflix
footer: Each year's bills buy NFLX at its avg price

vo.text: Every bill buys Netflix stock instead.
Price hike? Your investment goes up too.
Each year's bills buy at that year's average price.
You keep paying. It comes back.
About 8.7 times what Netflix charged you.

footerSteps.text: Each year's bills buy NFLX at its avg price

notes: Same inputs as teasers/v2/checks/06-pov-race.py (06b), recomputed: US Standard plan list price by month (Jul 2011 $7.99, May 2014 $8.99, Oct 2015 $9.99, Oct 2017 $10.99, Jan 2019 $12.99, Oct 2020 $13.99, Jan 2022 $15.49, Jan 2025 $17.99; Android Authority timeline, Variety 2019-01-15, CNBC 2025-01-21). Each year's 12 bills buy NFLX at that year's average split-adjusted close (Macrotrends); value = shares held × year-end close; a point at y + 0.99 is the Dec 31 close of year y. Bills 2012: 12 × $7.99 = $95.88 (÷ $1.19 avg = 80.6 shares); 2015: 9 × $8.99 + 3 × $9.99 = $110.88; total 2012-2025 $2,037.32. Shares 188.511 × $93.76 (12/31/2025 close, = StatMuse) = $17,674.75 → ≈ $17,700 (3 s.f.); footer step 188.5 × 93.76 = 17,673.76 ≈ $17,700. Multiple 17,674.75 ÷ 2,037.32 = 8.68 → ≈ 8.7×. 2013: NFLX close 5.26 ÷ 1.33 = 3.95 (quadruples). End 2020 $9,163.36 (passes $9,000 at x ≈ 2020.95, t ≈ 15.43). 2022: $10,390.18 → $5,279.03 (−49%, halves). Race clock: x 2012.0 → 2025.99 over t 2.0 → 23.0 s (1.50 s a year); purchase ticks land at t 2.0, 5.50, 7.63, 10.63, 12.51, 15.13, 17.01, 21.51. Netflix pays no dividend, so price-only is the total return. No fees or taxes.
